slides.texte_overlay:
why boredom is secretly
good for your brain

it sparks creativity

when your brain has nothing to do, it starts making its own ideas. many of the best thoughts arrive in the shower or on a walk, never while you're scrolling.

it resets your focus

constant stimulation trains your brain to need more and more. short bored moments teach it to calm down, so it can focus deeply again when it matters.

it shows what you want

boredom is a quiet signal that something in your life needs to change. listening to it instead of drowning it out often points you to what you really want.

it makes room for curiosity

a bored mind gets curious, and feeding that curiosity with something real beats another hour of scrolling. boredom is often curiosity knocking on the door.
slides.texte_sophia:
it makes room for curiosity

a bored mind gets curious. the Sophia app turns that into one short lesson a day, a planet or a painting, and 5 minutes of real curiosity beats another hour of scrolling.

slides.texte_overlay:
it lowers stress

doing nothing for a few minutes gives your nervous system a break from constant input. a little boredom each day is one of the simplest forms of rest there is.
